reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Same AI, separate source-first pass after freezing. Started with the TER tables, prerequisite chains and dated catalogue period evidence, reconstructed the nominal project and elective path, then evaluated the workbook evidence for drug action, biological mechanisms, laboratory methods, population evidence and treatment decisions. Rechecked every supported pairing and the specialist gaps against the frozen record.
findings: The programme-specific 2026–2027 TER appendices I–IV govern the 180 EC bachelor. The eponymous Pharmacy major is the broad route with the required scientific and practice curriculum. It contains the common 60 EC first year, the 60 EC second year, 45 compulsory EC in Year 3 including the 15 EC research project, and 15 EC of restricted Pharmacy electives. The Medical Pharmaceutical Sciences major differs by substituting a 30 EC minor for the six Year 3 specialist courses. The degree has English and Dutch instruction. The TER identifies courses taught mainly in Dutch. The Safe Microbiological Techniques certificate is earned through Pharmaceutical Microbiology and adds no credits.

Appendix IV requires Pharmaceutical Analysis before Bioanalysis and Instrumental Analysis. The cell practical and, where applicable, Physiology and Pharmacology or Biopharmacy 1 precede toxicology, microbiology, pharmacokinetics and Biopharmacy 2. Ocasys lists Microbiology and Biopharmacy 2 in paired rotation groups, so each is counted once, in separate teaching blocks. Molecules and Reactivity precedes the Organic Chemistry Practical. Physiology and Pharmacology and Receptor Pharmacology precede the Pharmacology Practical. In a valid nominal third year, complete the six required courses in the autumn, including enough early courses to exceed 130 EC four weeks before the Semester 2a project. Complete the 15 EC supervised project in 2a. A valid spread of restricted choices in the three separate 2b blocks is Advanced Human Disease Model Technologies, Pharmacology of Chronic Diseases and Ageing, and Herbal Medicine. This establishes feasible choice space without requiring those particular electives in the comparison.

The closest option has a substantive foundation in physiology, cell biology, biochemistry and laboratory work, and extends it through pathophysiology, immunity and drug action. Pharmacology supports target and receptor analysis, pharmacokinetics and selected therapies. The lab contributes aseptic work, susceptibility testing and molecular methods, and statistical and data courses supply methods for evaluating evidence. The second option retains epidemiology, pharmacology, health psychology and evidence synthesis. It uses social psychology and qualitative methods for patient experience, ethical persuasion for communication methods, and public economics for health policy, equity and social insurance. Moving Behavioral Economics to the final autumn resolves the sole offering conflict. Adding Human Physiology, Mechanisms of Disease and Public Economics grounds the second option in treatment context and public health. Communication and leadership are complementary, not pharmacist training. A discovery or formulation option was tested against the current course descriptions and enriched topics. Biochemistry, the life-science laboratory and Pharmacology address enzymes, biomolecules, molecular methods, drug targets and kinetics. These do not form a cumulative sequence in chemical synthesis, pharmaceutical assays, formulation, dosage forms or drug delivery. Data science cannot supply that missing specialist progression. The two options satisfy the pairwise floor and teach distinct approaches, with different empirical and scientific methods. Comparator-only components preserve important clinical, technology, chemistry and research gaps.
